items.note: Quasi-experiment with fourth graders (31 ChatGPT-feedback, 31 control) scored on a Creative Writing Product Evaluation Scale plus writing self-efficacy; non-random assignment.
Quasi-experiment with 29 fourth graders using AI image-visualization tools in creative writing; the only quantitative outcome is the Writing Disposition Scale (an attitude measure) plus interviews.

Thesis with two experiments comparing generative-AI and non-AI groups on brainstorming (originality, flexibility, fluency, elaboration) and on the Divergent Associations Task (originality, semantic distance); assignment and sample size not in the abstract.

Randomizes 331 participants to generic, partially personalized, or fully personalized LLM assistants for a marketing campaign task, with rated quality and creativity; AI-configuration comparison only (OSF preregistration planned a no-AI arm, check full text).
High-school classroom study with 34 students using synectics plus ChatGPT and 30 controls; creative writing ability improved, but how it was measured and how groups were formed are not stated.
Design workshops and interviews with 10 fashion students ideating with image-generating AI; experts rated originality and novelty against a control group; very small sample.

Middle-school design-thinking program with 57 students using generative AI in the Empathize stage and 60 without; creative problem-solving ability measured pre and post, possibly by a self-report scale; outcome likely measured without AI (after_ai).

Graduate engineering class of 33 students randomly organized into teams, with ChatGPT added to select teams for product brainstorming; student-perceived creativity of ideas and NLP homogeneity of ideas; how teams got ChatGPT is not stated; small sample.

Hong Kong secondary students randomly assigned to a five-week GenAI-driven storytelling intervention or traditional writing instruction; rubric-scored writing (including creativity) pre and post; whether the post-test was written without AI is not stated (abstract from the journal PDF).

Ten polytechnic students in two groups, one with ChatGPT, on the Alternative Uses Test and a creative storytelling task scored for fluency, flexibility, and originality; very small sample, assignment not stated.
